input.sql:
WITH r AS (SELECT po_id, count(*) nrec, sum(pounds) rlb, min(received_on::date) first_rec FROM erp_receipts GROUP BY po_id),
m AS (SELECT p.po_id, p.job_id, l.material, l.pounds, r.nrec, r.rlb,
 row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY p.job_id ORDER BY p.ordered_on, p.po_id) rn
 FROM erp_purchase_orders p JOIN erp_po_lines l USING(po_id) LEFT JOIN r USING(po_id) WHERE l.material <> 'outside processing'),
jf AS (SELECT job_id, max(CASE WHEN rn>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) has_fu FROM m GROUP BY job_id)
SELECT jf.has_fu, count(*) first_pos_received, sum(CASE WHEN m.nrec>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) multi_receipt,
 round(median(m.rlb/m.pounds),4) med_rec_over_po, round(quantile_cont(m.rlb/m.pounds,0.1),4) p10, round(quantile_cont(m.rlb/m.pounds,0.9),4) p90,
 sum(CASE WHEN m.rlb > m.pounds*1.02 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over_2pct, sum(CASE WHEN m.rlb < m.pounds*0.98 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) under_2pct
FROM m JOIN jf USING(job_id) WHERE m.rn=1 AND m.nrec IS NOT NULL AND m.pounds>0 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH r AS (SELECT DISTINCT po_id FROM erp_receipts),
m AS (SELECT p.po_id, p.job_id, p.ordered_on::date od, p.due_on::date dd, r.po_id IS NOT NULL rec,
 row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY p.job_id ORDER BY p.ordered_on, p.po_id) rn
 FROM erp_purchase_orders p JOIN erp_po_lines l USING(po_id) LEFT JOIN r USING(po_id) WHERE l.material <> 'outside processing'),
fu AS (SELECT job_id, min(od) first_fu_od, max(od) last_fu_od, max(dd) last_fu_due FROM m WHERE rn>1 GROUP BY job_id),
rw AS (SELECT job_id, min(work_date::date) first_rw, max(work_date::date) last_rw, count(*) n_rw FROM shop_labour_entries WHERE rework=1 GROUP BY job_id),
fp AS (SELECT p.job_id, min(rc.received_on::date) first_rec FROM m p JOIN erp_receipts rc USING(po_id) WHERE p.rn=1 GROUP BY 1)
SELECT count(*) fu_jobs, sum(CASE WHEN rw.job_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) no_rework,
 sum(CASE WHEN rw.first_rw < fu.first_fu_od THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) rework_before_fu_po,
 sum(CASE WHEN rw.first_rw >= fu.first_fu_od AND rw.first_rw < fu.last_fu_due THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) rework_before_due,
 sum(CASE WHEN rw.first_rw >= fu.last_fu_due THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) rework_after_due,
 median(rw.first_rw - fu.first_fu_od) med_days_po_to_rework,
 median(fu.last_fu_due - fu.first_fu_od) med_po_lead_days,
 median(j.completed_on::date - fu.last_fu_od) med_days_lastfu_to_complete,
 sum(CASE WHEN j.completed_on::date < fu.last_fu_due THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) completed_before_fu_due
FROM fu LEFT JOIN rw USING(job_id) JOIN erp_jobs j USING(job_id)

content.text:
I've saved `challenge.json`. My verdict is that F5 **stands with changes**.

**What held up**
- **Not duplicates.** I looked across jobs as well as within them: same vendor, same material, exact same pounds, on a different job. 3,207 unreceived POs have such a twin within 0–5 days, but 3,863 have one 30–35 days apart. Real duplicates would bunch up close in time, so these look like chance matches (q304).
- **Scrap-replacement buys.** Each follow-up PO still matches a scrap report on the same day, sized to the scrapped pieces.
- **No price premium.** Follow-ups cost the same per lb as the job's first PO (median ratio 1.0026, q310). The cost is the scrap itself, not pricing.

**What changed**
1. **The 132 "unreceived first POs" from Jan 2016 are really replacement buys.** They sit on jobs whose original PO is older than the records. Every one of the 30,802 scrap reports has an unreceived PO placed the same day (q284, q288). That makes the totals 30,802 POs and $2,366,230 over 2016–2025, about $236,623/yr. With the 86 Dec-2025 orders that aren't yet due, this accounts for all 30,888 unreceived material POs (q318, q321).
2. **The GL match proves nothing.** The ledger books material (and outside processing) exactly at PO dollars in the month the PO is placed, in all 120 months (q277). So the 1.0000 match is built in. It can't show the cost is real. If replacement POs went unfilled, GL material is overstated by up to $2.37M, which is the case F5 called "not an overstatement."
3. **"Shipped in full, so the material arrived" doesn't follow.** Rework starts the same day the replacement PO is placed, and before it's due, on 96.2% of jobs with follow-ups (q272). The pieces were re-run before the material could have arrived, so the shipment doesn't depend on it. My reading is that the re-runs used stock on hand. Whether the replacement material ever arrived is now an open question.
4. **Receipts can't settle it.** Received pounds equal PO pounds on every received first PO (q269), so the receipt record looks copied from the PO rather than weighed on arrival.
5. **Outside processing was left out.** All 1,234 outside-processing POs ($1,718,008) are unreceived, with one per job and no repeats (q314, q318). Receipts just aren't used for outside processing.

**Still unexplained:** why the scrap-material memo runs above my own valuation of scrap (q280). It doesn't bear on duplicates.

**What would settle it:** vendor invoices or AP records for a sample of replacement POs from vendors 1, 3 and 4. They would show whether the material was billed and delivered, and so whether the $2.37M is real scrap cost or an overstated ledger.
